subject: Biology
title: Photosynthesis in Higher Plants
summary: Photosynthesis is the basis of autotrophic nutrition: it converts light energy into chemical energy: 6CO₂ + 12H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6H₂O + 6O₂. It happens in chloroplasts — light reactions in the grana (thylakoids), dark (biosynthetic) reactions in the stroma.
Light reactions split water, release O₂ and make ATP and NADPH through the Z-scheme (non-cyclic photophosphorylation). ATP is made by chemiosmosis.
The Calvin cycle (C₃ pathway) fixes CO₂ with RuBisCO onto RuBP; C₄ plants (maize, sugarcane) first fix CO₂ with PEP carboxylase in mesophyll cells and have Kranz anatomy, avoiding photorespiration.
The rate of photosynthesis depends on light, CO₂, temperature and water — Blackman's law of limiting factors.

formulas.name: Overall equation
formulas.mistake: The O₂ released comes from water, not CO₂ (Cornelius van Niel; confirmed with ¹⁸O).

formulas.name: Early experiments
formulas.formula: Priestley (1770): plants restore air (mouse and candle);  Ingenhousz: needs sunlight, only green parts;  Sachs (1854): glucose made, stored as starch;  Engelmann: action spectrum with Cladophora and aerobic bacteria (blue and red light)

formulas.name: Pigments
formulas.formula: chlorophyll a (bright/blue-green, main pigment, reaction centre);  chlorophyll b (yellow-green);  xanthophylls (yellow);  carotenoids (yellow-orange) — accessory pigments that also protect chlorophyll from photo-oxidation

formulas.name: Photosystems
formulas.formula: PS I reaction centre P700;  PS II reaction centre P680;  LHC (antenna) of hundreds of pigment molecules

formulas.name: Photolysis of water
formulas.formula: 2H₂O → 4H⁺ + O₂ + 4e⁻ (on the inner side of thylakoid membrane, linked to PS II; Mn, Cl⁻ needed)

formulas.name: Non-cyclic vs cyclic photophosphorylation
formulas.formula: non-cyclic: PS II + PS I, gives ATP + NADPH + O₂ (Z-scheme);  cyclic: only PS I, gives only ATP, in stroma lamellae (no NADP reductase there)

formulas.name: Chemiosmosis
formulas.formula: proton gradient across thylakoid membrane (high H⁺ in lumen) → H⁺ flow through CF₀ to CF₁ of ATP synthase → ATP

formulas.name: Calvin cycle
formulas.formula: carboxylation: RuBP + CO₂ → 2 × 3-PGA (RuBisCO);  reduction: uses ATP + NADPH;  regeneration of RuBP

formulas.name: C₄ (Hatch–Slack) pathway
formulas.formula: PEP (3C) + CO₂ → OAA (4C) by PEP carboxylase in mesophyll → malate/aspartate → bundle sheath → releases CO₂ for Calvin cycle → pyruvate back to mesophyll
formulas.when: C₄ plants: maize, sugarcane, sorghum, Amaranthus.

formulas.name: Kranz anatomy
formulas.formula: large bundle sheath cells around vascular bundles, many chloroplasts, thick walls impervious to gas, no intercellular spaces

formulas.name: Photorespiration
formulas.formula: RuBisCO binds O₂: RuBP + O₂ → phosphoglycerate + phosphoglycolate; no sugar, no ATP — wasteful; in chloroplast, peroxisome and mitochondria
formulas.when: Why C₄ plants are more efficient.
formulas.note: C₄ plants have no photorespiration because CO₂ concentration around RuBisCO is high.

formulas.name: Blackman's law of limiting factors (1905)
formulas.formula: if a process depends on several factors, its rate is set by the factor nearest its minimal value

examples.title: ATP and NADPH count
examples.problem: How many ATP and NADPH are needed to make one glucose in the Calvin cycle?
examples.solution: One CO₂ per turn needs 3 ATP + 2 NADPH, and glucose needs 6 turns: 18 ATP and 12 NADPH.

examples.title: ATP in C₄ plants
examples.problem: C₄ plants need 2 extra ATP per CO₂ (to regenerate PEP). ATP for one glucose?

examples.title: Source of O₂
examples.problem: How was it shown that the O₂ released comes from water?
examples.solution: Van Niel's work on purple and green sulphur bacteria suggested H₂O is the hydrogen donor (like H₂S); later experiments with ¹⁸O-labelled water showed the O₂ came from water.

examples.title: First stable product
examples.problem: What is the first stable product in C₃ and C₄ plants?

examples.title: Limiting factor in a greenhouse
examples.problem: Why are tomatoes and bell peppers grown in CO₂-enriched greenhouses?
examples.solution: CO₂ is often the main limiting factor; raising it (up to about 0.05%) increases the rate of photosynthesis and the yield of C₃ plants.

examples.title: Cyclic photophosphorylation location
examples.problem: Where does cyclic photophosphorylation take place, and why?
examples.solution: In the stroma lamellae, which have PS I but lack PS II and NADP reductase — so electrons cycle back and only ATP is made.

topics.title: Site of photosynthesis
topics.explain: Chloroplasts in mesophyll cells line up along walls to get optimum light. Membranes (grana) trap light and make ATP and NADPH; the stroma has enzymes that reduce CO₂ to sugars (light-independent or dark reactions).

topics.title: Action and absorption spectra
topics.explain: Chlorophyll a absorbs most in blue and red regions; the action spectrum of photosynthesis closely matches the absorption spectrum of chlorophyll a, but other pigments also contribute.

topics.title: Electron transport
topics.explain: PS II absorbs 680 nm light; excited electrons pass via plastoquinone, cytochromes b6f and plastocyanin to PS I; PS I re-excites them at 700 nm and passes them to ferredoxin and NADP⁺ reductase to make NADPH. Electrons lost by PS II are replaced by water splitting.

topics.title: Proton gradient
topics.explain: The gradient forms because protons from water splitting accumulate in the lumen, protons are moved into the lumen as electrons pass through the cytochrome complex, and NADP reductase removes protons from the stroma when making NADPH.

topics.title: Factors affecting photosynthesis
topics.explain: Light: rate rises with intensity at low light, saturates at about 10% of full sunlight. CO₂: C₃ plants respond to higher CO₂ more than C₄ (C₄ saturate at ~360 ppm). Temperature: C₄ plants have a higher optimum. Water stress closes stomata and reduces leaf surface.

topics.title: C₃ vs C₄ comparison
topics.explain: C₄ plants tolerate higher temperatures, show greater productivity, have lower CO₂ compensation points and no photorespiration. In C₄ plants RuBisCO is only in bundle sheath cells; PEP carboxylase only in mesophyll.

ratta: PS I = P700;  PS II = P680.
Non-cyclic: ATP + NADPH + O₂;  cyclic: only ATP (stroma lamellae).
C₃ first product 3-PGA;  C₄ first product OAA.
Photorespiration: RuBisCO + O₂, wasteful, absent in C₄.
